html:
Bahrain became fully independent in August 1971, when its treaties with Britain ended. A year before, a United Nations mission had found that Bahrainis wanted their own state, not union with Iran.

Since the 1800s Bahrain had been under British protection, which ran its foreign affairs. When Britain announced in 1968 that it would leave the Gulf, Iran revived its old claim to the islands. The UN survey of 1970, approved by the Security Council in Resolution 278, settled the question, and Iran accepted it.

Bahrain talked of joining the other sheikhdoms in the United Arab Emirates but chose to go alone, as did Qatar. The Al Khalifa ruler took the title of emir, and later king.
